title: Pete Hegseth Nominated as Defense Secretary
description_short: Pete Hegseth Nominated as Defense Secretary
description_medium: Trump nominated Pete Hegseth, a Fox News host with no senior government or military leadership experience, as Secretary of Defense. Shortly after the nomination, allegations of a past sexual assault surfaced, which Hegseth denied, though he admitted to paying a settlement. The nomination raised serious concerns about the politicization of the military and the fitness of Trump's cabinet picks.
description_long: On November 12, 2024, Donald Trump announced Pete Hegseth as his nominee for secretary of defense. Hegseth was then a Fox News host and had served in the Army National Guard, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, but had not held senior civilian or military leadership posts. The nomination put a high-stakes national-security department in the hands of a public commentator with limited experience overseeing a large bureaucracy. Soon after the announcement, reporting brought forward a past sexual-assault allegation. Hegseth denied the allegation and acknowledged paying a settlement. The accusation and settlement became part of the scrutiny surrounding his nomination, while neither fact alone establishes the allegation's truth. The choice also prompted questions about the criteria Trump used for a cabinet role responsible for the armed forces, military readiness, and defense policy. The nomination drew attention to the tension between Hegseth's media profile and the management experience ordinarily associated with the post.
